title: Writer handoff: fence the previous epoch before accepting replacement writes
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Transfer writer epochs; stale writers must not regain authority.
sourceAcceptance: Only the authorized epoch writes; stale writers are rejected and acknowledged data is retained.
preconditions: Local browser HTML, CSS and JavaScript only; no server or account.
Two fixed effects were acknowledged at writer-old epoch 41 before the handoff.
The replacement presents writer-new epoch 42; authorization checks both writer identity and epoch.
A confirmed receipt is an assumed atomic authoritative revocation/grant fixture, not a fencing protocol implementation.
The unsafe fixture intentionally leaves both grants active and accepts stale-grant regression.
An unavailable receipt supplies no authoritative ownership or stale-write observation.
actions: Select one authority receipt fixture and one acknowledged-data readback fixture.
Begin with two already acknowledged effects, then transfer authority.
Probe the replacement, delayed old writer and replacement identity with a stale epoch.
Replay the previous writer grant and attempt another old-epoch write.
Verify authorization, fencing order, no regained authority and retained original effects.
Check a learning prediction independently; inspect full retained proof or explicitly reset.
assertions: Confirmed fencing precedes the replacement write; only writer-new@42 accepts a post-transfer effect.
Delayed writer-old@41, wrong-epoch writer-new@41 and replayed writer-old@41 are rejected.
Replaying an old grant cannot regress confirmed authority or its epoch high-water mark.
Both original acknowledged IDs, payloads and exact-once effect counts remain intact.
Known safety or retention violations yield FAIL; unavailable authority evidence without a known failure yields UNKNOWN.
Correct learning predictions never turn a failed or unknown handoff into PASS.
Strict inputs, ordered lifecycle, immutable detached snapshots and six-attempt retained history remain guarded.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine behavioral RED and before implementation

testRuntime.purpose: Existing Node22 tooling only; not production Node24 validation.

limits: Every write, authority receipt, data fault and effect is deterministic synthetic data.
No actual database epochs, leases, durable fencing, concurrent writers or acknowledged-data durability certification.
No Azure management calls, identity, credentials, IaC, deployment, expenditure, new packages or framework.
Known-effect ledger counts never establish total effects when outcomes are unknown.
Expected stale-write rejection is a negative safety probe, not uninterrupted user-migration proof.
History exists only in browser memory until explicit reset or reload, with a hard six-attempt cap.
No production Node24, native host, source-parent completion, five-nines or platform guarantee.
The abandoned browser lifecycle prototype is unqualified; no unattended-runner certification.
B-S069 and original D-S069 native acceptance remain separate and unfulfilled.
One frozen S unit only; tests, plumbing, evidence and refinement earn no additional units.
